costDetail: No cost from network providers or suppliers; non-network purchases may need reimbursement capped at the allowable amount.
eligibility: TRICARE beneficiaries; the page says eligibility begins at 27 weeks of pregnancy and covers mothers who legally adopt an infant and plan to breastfeed.
whenNote: Official page says eligibility starts at 27 weeks of pregnancy.
catches: Batteries, travel bags, cleaning supplies, nursing bras and warranties are not covered. Hospital-grade rentals need a referral and authorization.
notes: Supply limits listed: 100 storage bags per 30 days, 2 bottles and 2 locking rings per 12 months, 1 valve set per month for 12 months.

name: UPMC for You Baby Steps baby gift
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who finish the Baby Steps program can pick a free baby gift bundle.
freeStuff: A baby gift bundle for members who complete Baby Steps.
valueBasis: One portable crib or car seat equivalent at about $80 to $100
costDetail: Members of UPMC for You only.
eligibility: UPMC for You members who join Baby Steps before 34 weeks and start prenatal care before 13 weeks.
whenNote: Join before 34 weeks of pregnancy.
catches: Must join by 34 weeks, keep calls and prenatal tests. Gift format changed over the years (car seat, stroller, play yard, now an online bundle).
notes: Eligibility set by the Baby Steps health coach.

name: Vaccines for Children program
whatYouGet: Free childhood vaccines, including RSV antibody nirsevimab, for children who are Medicaid-eligible, uninsured, underinsured or American Indian/Alaska Native.
freeStuff: Free childhood vaccines for eligible babies.
costDetail: Vaccine is free; the office may charge a visit fee.
eligibility: Children 18 and under in the listed groups.
whenNote: Vaccines begin at birth and through childhood.
catches: Underinsured children only get it at community health centers; CHIP-only children do not qualify. Ask the doctor to confirm they take VFC.

name: Virtual lactation consultant covered by insurance
whatYouGet: Online visits with a lactation consultant, billed to insurance where your plan covers them.
valueBasis: One lactation visit at about $100 to $200 paid by the plan
costDetail: Site says most plans cover visits at no cost; confirm with your plan.
eligibility: Members of an accepted insurance plan.
catches: Coverage is not guaranteed; Medicaid and out-of-network rules vary.
notes: Seen only in official-domain search results.

name: Virtual lactation consultations
whatYouGet: Video visits with a lactation consultant, billed to insurance where your plan covers them.
valueBasis: One lactation visit at about $100 to $200 paid by the plan
costDetail: The site says most commercial plans cover visits at 100% with no copay; Medicaid and self-funded plans vary.
eligibility: Members of a covered insurance plan; discounted self-pay rates exist for others.
catches: Coverage is not guaranteed; some plans need prior authorization or a referral.
notes: Coverage claim comes from the provider, not an insurer.

name: WellCare of North Carolina Better Beginnings rewards
whatYouGet: Medicaid members who notify the plan of pregnancy earn $25 for a prenatal visit and $25 for a postpartum visit, plus a choice of stroller, play yard, car seat or diapers.
freeStuff: Rewards plus a stroller, play yard, car seat or diapers for members who attend a prenatal visit.
valueBasis: $25 to $50 in rewards plus one item such as a play yard at about $80 to $100
costDetail: Members of the plan only.
eligibility: WellCare of NC Medicaid members who submit a Notification of Pregnancy.
whenNote: Notify the plan during pregnancy; reward follows a prenatal visit.
catches: Must notify the plan before the birth. Up to $75 a year in rewards. A New Parent package and free pump are also mentioned; confirm with the plan.
notes: South Carolina and Georgia WellCare pages exist but are older and not included.

name: Wellpoint Medicaid baby essentials gift card
whatYouGet: Washington members can get a $100 gift card for baby items, and West Virginia members up to $170 after six prenatal visits.
freeStuff: A gift card for baby items for Wellpoint Medicaid members.
valueBasis: Plan pages state $100 (WA) and up to $170 (WV)
costDetail: Members of the plan only.
eligibility: Wellpoint Medicaid members in WA or WV who complete required visits.
whenNote: Card is earned through prenatal visits.
catches: One card per pregnancy. Anthem Ohio offers a choice of two items; amounts on some Anthem pages are old.
notes: Healthy Rewards line seen: 888-990-8681.

whatYouGet: Confidential help finding local resources for paying bills, food, housing, utilities, healthcare and other needs: call 2-1-1 and a local expert connects you to services. National Diaper Bank Network's page also points families to 2-1-1 for diaper assistance.
costDetail: Page does not state a cost; the service is a referral line, not a benefit itself.
eligibility: Anyone.
catches: Resources and what they offer vary by local 211 service; 2-1-1 refers you to programs rather than providing items itself.
notes: Fetched directly: home page says every call is completely confidential and links to local 211 lookup. Not baby-specific.

name: Early Head Start (services for pregnant women)
whatYouGet: Early Head Start programs may serve pregnant women and expectant families.
costDetail: Free
eligibility: Pregnant women with family income at or below the federal poverty line, or receiving TANF, SSI or SNAP; only programs that serve pregnant women (some Early Head Start programs, including the home-based option) enroll them.
whenNote: Head Start says a pregnant woman can follow the same steps to enroll herself; not every program serves pregnant women.
catches: Not every program serves pregnant women; waiting lists possible.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. headstart.gov returned 403 to automated fetching; official-domain search results say apply by contacting a local program (Head Start Center Locator or toll-free line 1-866-763-6481) and that waitlists are common.

name: Every Baby Sleeps Safe portable crib
whatYouGet: A free portable crib kit with a fitted sheet and safe sleep education, given by a local Cribs for Kids partner.
freeStuff: A free portable crib kit if you qualify.
valueBasis: One portable crib at about $80 shelf price
costDetail: Free while funding lasts
eligibility: Ohio families at least 32 weeks pregnant or with a baby under 1 year, with low income (partners use 100% to 185% of poverty guidelines; one page says under 200%); must attend a safe sleep education session.
whenNote: The program starts at 32 weeks of pregnancy.
catches: While quantities last. Partner list in the results dates from 2023, so confirm with a county partner.
notes: Official-domain search results only.

name: Find a Crib
whatYouGet: Free portable crib and safe sleep education through local partners.
freeStuff: A portable crib and safe sleep teaching from a local partner, if you qualify.
valueBasis: One portable crib at about $80 shelf price
costDetail: Free through partner organizations
eligibility: Financial need, infant 12 months or younger, and receiving safe sleep education (per search result); each partner sets its own criteria; crib limits 30 lb and 35 in.
whenNote: Infant must be 12 months or younger; some local partners start before the birth.
catches: Some partners provide education only; availability varies. One Cribs for Kids partner document says the program is not a free crib giveaway, so local partners set the terms.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. Site returned 403 to automated fetching, so this rests on official-domain search results. Search results say you find the nearest partner on the site map and call to apply; if you are not eligible the site suggests Healthy Start or local health departments.

name: Get a Car Seat Checked
whatYouGet: Free car seat inspection events and a search for certified child passenger safety technicians who check installation and teach you to install it yourself.
costDetail: Safe Kids coalitions host 8,000+ free inspection events
eligibility: Anyone with a child car seat.
whenNote: Get the seat checked before the first ride home from the hospital.
catches: Inspection and education only; not a free car seat. The page says events are free but does not say whether individual technicians or inspection stations charge. Availability depends on local events and technicians.
notes: Fetched directly: page says Safe Kids coalitions host more than 8,000 free car seat inspection events and lists three ways to find a certified technician (events, the technician search, NHTSA's directory). Bring the car seat and vehicle manuals; you install the seat yourself with guidance.

name: Get Help Now / Member Diaper Banks
whatYouGet: Directs families to local diaper assistance via 2-1-1 and a directory of member diaper banks that distribute free diapers.
freeStuff: Free diapers from a local diaper bank, if one near you serves your family.
costDetail: Free diapers from local diaper banks
eligibility: Families in need; each local program sets its own rules.
catches: Availability varies by community; NDBN does not distribute diapers directly.
notes: Fetched directly. Per the page: call 2-1-1 or search 211.org for diapers or basic needs, check listings under children, try faith-based groups and food pantries, or use the member diaper bank directory at /member-directory/.

name: Good Neighbor car seat checkups
whatYouGet: Car seat checkup events in some cities where new car seats are given to families in need.
freeStuff: A new car seat at some events if you are in need.
costDetail: Seats go to those in need; some local coalitions may charge a fee for a seat
eligibility: Families in need attending an event; events are city by city.
whenNote: Seat is needed for the first ride home.
catches: Event dates and cities are limited. Safe Kids says a local coalition may charge a fee for a seat.
notes: Official-domain search results only; no rules for who gets a seat were shown.

name: Healthy Start
whatYouGet: Community projects offering care coordination, education and support before, during and after pregnancy.
costDetail: Free through local projects
eligibility: Pregnant women, new parents, children to 18 months and partners in a funded service area.
whenNote: Serves pregnant women, partners and babies up to 18 months.
catches: Only in funded communities.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. hrsa.gov and mchb.hrsa.gov returned 403; official-domain search results say projects have different enrollment guidelines, you must live in a served area, and the HRSA page lists a site finder.

name: Mississippi Safe Riders Magnolia
whatYouGet: Car seat distribution for low-income households applied for through an online form.
freeStuff: A car seat for qualifying Mississippi families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
costDetail: Free for qualifying households.
eligibility: Low-income households or those receiving federal aid.
whenNote: Apply before the baby arrives.
catches: Details thinly shown; confirm with injuryprevention@msdh.ms.gov.

name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
whatYouGet: Free, confidential, 24/7 call or text support from a counselor for people who are pregnant or new parents; 1-833-852-6262 (1-833-TLC-MAMA).
costDetail: Free and confidential
eligibility: Anyone pregnant, postpartum or a family member; English and Spanish, and interpreter support in more than 60 languages.
catches: Some HRSA pages in the results are old. Counselors are not all licensed clinicians.
notes: Official-domain search results only. TTY: dial 711 then the number.

name: Nurse-Family Partnership home visits
whatYouGet: Free visits from a registered nurse during pregnancy and until the child is 2, covering breastfeeding, nutrition, safe sleep and development.
costDetail: Pages say the services are completely free
eligibility: First-time moms who meet an income rule and are about 28 weeks pregnant or less (a second page says under 29 weeks); local agency sets details and area.
whenNote: Enrollment is open only up to about 28 weeks of pregnancy; the site says enroll as soon as you know.
catches: Only where a local agency serves your area. The income figure was not in the results. The site is now branded Changent.
notes: Official-domain search results only; pages are several years old.

name: PSI HelpLine
whatYouGet: Free, confidential helpline for perinatal mental health support and resources; call or text 800-944-4773 (Spanish text 971-203-7773), leave a message and a trained volunteer returns your call or text.
costDetail: Free and confidential
eligibility: Anyone; no diagnosis needed.
catches: Not for emergencies; response times vary (search results cite business-hours return, and up to about 48 hours on the Spanish page).
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. postpartum.net returned 403 to automated fetching; details from official-domain search results. In crisis call or text 988.

name: Texas Safe Riders child safety seats
brand: Texas Department of State Health Services
whatYouGet: Free or low-cost car seats for low-income families after an education session.
freeStuff: A free car seat for qualifying Texas families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
costDetail: Free for qualifying families.
eligibility: Low-income families or those with financial hardship; caregivers attend a class.
whenNote: Get the seat before the baby is born.
catches: Call 800-252-8255 for a site; seat supply depends on the site.

name: Virginia seat distribution program
whatYouGet: Free child car seats for families that qualify by income, given out at local sites.
freeStuff: A free car seat for income-eligible Virginia families.
valueBasis: One infant car seat at about $100
costDetail: Free; class may be required.
eligibility: Parents eligible for WIC, SNAP, Medicaid, TANF or FAMIS with a child 7 or younger.
whenNote: Get the seat before the hospital trip home.
catches: Call 1-800-732-8333 to find a local site.

name: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children)
whatYouGet: Healthy foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support and referrals for pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants and children under 5.
freeStuff: A monthly food package or food benefit, including fruit and vegetables, for pregnant and postpartum women and infants who qualify.
valueBasis: USDA states $48 a month in fruit and vegetable benefit for pregnant participants (FY 2026); counted for 6 to 12 months; other foods and formula not counted
costDetail: Foods provided at no cost; apply through a local WIC agency
eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months) or breastfeeding women, infants and children under 5; income at or below 185% of the federal poverty guidelines (or on Medicaid, SNAP or TANF), live in the state, and a nutrition-risk check. The 2026-27 limit is $29,526 for one person and $40,034 for two, plus $10,508 per added person; an expected birth counts as a household member.
region: US (apply through your state or local WIC agency)
whenNote: WIC serves pregnant women, so applying early in pregnancy gives the most months of benefit.
catches: Requires an appointment with a local WIC agency; bring ID, proof of address and proof of income or program enrollment as the agency instructs.
notes: Steps: 1) Use the Eligibility Tool. 2) Contact your local WIC agency by phone or online to start. 3) Attend an in-person or virtual appointment. fns.usda.gov now redirects to fna.usda.gov (Food and Nutrition Administration).

name: WIC breastfeeding support and enhanced food package
whatYouGet: WIC breastfeeding mothers can get a peer counselor and an enhanced food package, and many WIC offices lend or give breast pumps.
freeStuff: Extra WIC food, a peer counselor and often a breast pump for breastfeeding mothers.
costDetail: Free for WIC participants.
eligibility: WIC participants who breastfeed; pump rules and peer counselor access vary by state.
whenNote: Fully breastfeeding mothers can keep the package until the baby is 12 months old.
catches: 63% of state agencies set conditions for a single-user electric pump; peer counselors are not available everywhere. Food amounts differ between two USDA pages.
notes: Extra to the usda-wic entry; fully breastfeeding mothers get more food for up to 12 months.

name: WIC Farmers Market Nutrition Program
whatYouGet: Coupons for fresh fruits, vegetables and herbs at approved farmers markets, issued on top of regular WIC benefits.
freeStuff: Farmers market produce coupons for WIC participants.
valueBasis: USDA says $10 to $30 a year per person federally
costDetail: Free for WIC participants.
eligibility: WIC-certified women, infants over 4 months and children; offered only by participating states.
whenNote: Issued to certified WIC participants, including pregnant women.
catches: Not every state or local agency runs it. Federal benefit is $10 to $30 a year; states may add more.
notes: Ask the local WIC office.

name: BabySteps Savings Plan
whatYouGet: A $50 seed deposit when you open a new MEFA U.Fund 529 for a baby within a year of birth or adoption.
freeStuff: $50 deposit into a new 529 account.
valueBasis: $50 seed deposit stated by the program
costDetail: No fee or minimum to open the account.
eligibility: Massachusetts resident child; open a new U.Fund 529 before the first birthday or adoption anniversary.
whenNote: Open the account before the child's first birthday.
catches: Must open a new account; it cannot be added to an existing 529. Deposit arrives about 6 weeks later. SNAP families get an extra $120 for a child under 1 (separate program, not entered here).
notes: Opt-out window of 30 days after opening.

name: Bridge Project cash stipend (Multnomah County)
whatYouGet: A $1,125 prenatal stipend, then $750 a month for 15 months and $375 a month for 21 months, for people selected by lottery.
costDetail: Free; research study with a lottery.
eligibility: Pregnant, 27 weeks or fewer (priority for 20 to 27 weeks), household income under $39,000, living in Multnomah County. 100 slots.
whenNote: Must apply at 27 weeks of pregnancy or earlier.
catches: Applications were set to open February 4, 2026; the results did not say whether slots remain. A lottery, so most applicants may get nothing.
notes: Left value null because selection is a draw. NYC Bridge Project phase has no current application; Philadelphia Joy Bank only seen on a news site.

name: California Paid Family Leave and SDI pregnancy disability
whatYouGet: Partial pay for up to 8 weeks to bond with a new child (Paid Family Leave), plus State Disability Insurance pay for the pregnancy and recovery period.
valueBasis: 8 weeks of bonding at half the $1,765 weekly maximum; actual pay depends on wages
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Worked in California and paid into State Disability Insurance in the base period (about 5 to 18 months before the claim). Pay is about 70% to 90% of wages depending on income, up to the maximum.
whenNote: Disability claims can start up to 4 weeks before the due date; bonding leave must fall within 1 year of birth.
catches: Weekly maximum shown by EDD is $1,765 (minimum $50), but one result did not say which year it starts. The first 7 days of a disability claim are unpaid. Bonding benefits are only in the first year after birth. Some results gave 4 weeks before and 6 to 8 weeks after birth for pregnancy disability.
notes: Pregnancy disability value is not counted in the estimate.

name: California Young Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A refundable state tax credit of up to $1,189 per return (tax year 2025) for filers with a child under 6, on top of the CalEITC.
valueBasis: Up to $1,189 per return for tax year 2025; $0 above the income limit
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the California return with form FTB 3514.
eligibility: Qualify for CalEITC with a child younger than 6 on Dec 31; earned income generally $32,900 or less (phase-out starts at $27,425). The child may have an ITIN instead of an SSN.
whenNote: Claimed on the state return for the year of the birth.
catches: The amount is per return, not per child, and shrinks as earnings pass $27,425.
notes: Latest year shown is 2025 ($1,154 in 2024).

name: CalKIDS newborn account
whatYouGet: An automatic $100 deposit for every child born in California on or after July 1, 2023, with small bonuses for claiming and linking a 529.
freeStuff: $100 deposited into a CalKIDS account for the baby.
valueBasis: $100 deposit plus $25 for claiming and $50 for linking a 529
costDetail: No cost; no contribution needed.
eligibility: Child born in California on or after July 1, 2023, any income.
whenNote: Claim up to 90 days after birth.
catches: Claim at calkids.org with the birth-certificate Local Registration Number or letter code. Wait up to 90 days after birth. Extra $25 for claiming online and $50 for linking a ScholarShare 529 (up to $175 total).
notes: Results disagreed on whether newborns get $500; the program FAQ and annual report say $500 is for eligible students, so I used $100.

name: CHET Baby Scholars (Connecticut)
whatYouGet: A one-time $100 contribution into a CHET Direct 529 account opened by the child's first birthday.
freeStuff: $100 deposit into a 529 account.
valueBasis: $100 contribution stated by the Treasurer
costDetail: No cost; no deposit stated as needed.
eligibility: Connecticut resident; one $100 per child regardless of the number of accounts.
whenNote: Open the account by the first birthday or within a year of adoption.
catches: A 2025 bill (SB 1462) would have ended the program, and the results did not show whether it passed. The older $150 second payment is no longer offered per a 2025 bill summary.
notes: Confirm with the Treasurer's office.

name: Child and Dependent Care Credit and dependent care FSA
whatYouGet: A tax credit for child care costs so you can work, or tax-free dependent care FSA money through an employer.
valueBasis: 20% to 50% of the $3,000 expense cap for one child, only if you pay for care
costDetail: No fee to claim, but it only pays back part of the child care you pay for. The credit is claimed on Form 2441; the FSA is offered by some employers.
eligibility: Work-related care for a child under 13; credit is 20% to 50% of up to $3,000 of expenses for one child, depending on income. FSA is only if your employer offers it.
whenNote: Applies in the years you pay for child care.
catches: Employer FSA exclusion is $7,500 for 2026 ($3,750 if married filing separately), which uses up the amount for the credit. Only applies if you pay for child care.
notes: Max credit $600 to $1,500 for one child is my estimate from the IRS rate and cap; IRS states the $3,000 cap and the 20% to 50% range.

name: Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A federal tax credit of $2,200 per qualifying child under 17 for tax year 2026, partly refundable.
valueBasis: $2,200 per child for tax year 2026, of which up to $1,700 is refundable
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the federal tax return (Schedule 8812).
eligibility: Child under 17 at year end with a Social Security number valid for work, issued by the return due date (including extensions). Full credit up to $200,000 income ($400,000 joint); refundable part needs $2,500 earned income. A child without the SSN can still bring the $500 Credit for Other Dependents.
whenNote: A baby born in late 2026 is first claimed on the 2026 return filed in 2027. A baby born in early 2027 is first claimed on the 2027 return, filed in 2028. The baby needs a Social Security number by the filing due date.
catches: The $2,200 figure is for tax year 2026; the 2027 amount is not known yet. The refundable part is capped at $1,700 per child. Not tax advice.
notes: Updated from 2025 ($2,200) to the 2026 figure shown in IRS Schedule 8812 and Form 1040-ES search results.

name: CollegeBound Starter
whatYouGet: A $100 starter bonus in a CollegeBound Saver account for children born to or adopted by Rhode Island families.
freeStuff: $100 deposit into a 529 account.
valueBasis: $100 starter bonus stated by the program
costDetail: Free, no minimum to start.
eligibility: Rhode Island child; open an account within a year of birth or adoption.
whenNote: Open the account before the first birthday.
catches: Replaced the older CollegeBoundbaby grant on July 1, 2021. Deposit about 45 to 60 days after opening. Results described it as a chance to receive the bonus; confirm terms.
notes: Not the old $100 CollegeBoundbaby, which covered 2015 to mid-2021 births.

name: Colorado FAMLI paid family leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay to bond with a new child (up to 4 more with pregnancy or birth complications), and up to 12 weeks of neonatal care leave for a baby in a NICU.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,448.02 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Earned at least $2,500 in Colorado in the past year. From July 1, 2026 the maximum is $1,448.02 a week: 90% of the first $804.46 of weekly wage, 50% above that.
whenNote: Give 30 days' notice when possible; the application can start up to 30 days before leave.
catches: Apply on the My FAMLI+ portal. A claim started before the birth stays a draft until proof of birth is uploaded. Bonding leave cannot start until a neonatal claim ends.

name: Connecticut Paid Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay in 12 months to bond with a new child: 95% of weekly wage up to $677.60, plus 60% of the excess, capped at $1,016.40 a week (2026).
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,016.40 weekly cap
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Connecticut workers who paid into the program. Pay is based on the two highest quarters of the base period.
whenNote: Leave must be used within 12 months of the birth.
catches: Pays money but does not give job protection (that comes from FMLA). Apply online or by phone; proof such as a hospital discharge paper or birth certificate is needed.

name: CT Baby Bonds
whatYouGet: A state-funded investment of $3,200 (the state says up to) for babies whose birth was covered by HUSKY, for use at ages 18 to 30.
freeStuff: $3,200 invested by the state for the child.
valueBasis: $3,200 investment stated by the state; paid out only at ages 18 to 30
costDetail: No application; enrolled automatically.
eligibility: Child born on or after July 1, 2023 whose birth was covered by HUSKY (Connecticut Medicaid). Parent immigration status does not matter.
whenNote: Automatic after a HUSKY-covered birth.
catches: Money is used later, for a Connecticut home, business, education or retirement, after financial literacy training. Pages differ on flat $3,200 vs up to $3,200.
notes: The state projects growth to $11,000 to $24,000; not used as the value.

name: DC Paid Family Leave
whatYouGet: Paid parental leave to bond with a new child: 90% of wages up to 1.5 times DC minimum wage and 50% above that, with a $1,100 weekly maximum.
valueBasis: 8 weeks (lower of 8 or 12) at half the $1,100 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Workers covered by a DC employer under the Paid Family Leave Act and meeting its earnings rules.
catches: Official DC pages say 12 weeks of parental leave; an older DOES one-pager says 8. The lower figure (8) is used for the estimate. Medical and family-caregiving leave were cut on Oct. 1, 2026, not parental leave.
notes: Application timing was not in the results.

name: Delaware Paid Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of parental leave pay at 80% of average weekly wage, capped at $900 a week; benefits began January 1, 2026.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $900 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Employer with 10 or more employees (employers with 10 to 24 may offer a minimum of 6 weeks until 2031), 12 months with the employer, 1,250 hours in the past year, and mostly working in Delaware.
whenNote: Apply as soon as you know you need leave; if unforeseen, within 30 days after the first day of leave.
catches: The first payment takes about 2 weeks to process. The signup URL is the state claims guide; the apply page was not named in the results.

name: Earned Income Tax Credit (with a child)
whatYouGet: A refundable federal tax credit for working families with income below set limits, larger with a qualifying child.
valueBasis: $0 above the income limit; up to the $4,427 IRS maximum for one child in tax year 2026 for lower earners
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the federal tax return.
eligibility: Earned income and AGI under the limit for filing status and children. For tax year 2026 with one child: $51,593 ($58,863 married filing jointly); investment income up to $12,200. The child and the filer need valid Social Security numbers.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born or lives with you; a baby born in 2027 counts on the 2027 return filed in 2028.
catches: Maximum for 2026 is $4,427 with one child; the actual amount shrinks as income rises and many families get less. The 2026 limits come from an IRS eligibility questionnaire and Notice 797 (shown as Rev. December 2026), not the main 2026 tables page. Form 8862 may be needed after a past denial.
notes: valueLow of 0 is deliberate: the credit is 0 for families over the limit. 2025 limit was $50,434 ($57,554 joint) per Publication 596.

name: Empire State Child Credit (New York)
whatYouGet: A refundable state credit of $1,000 per child under 4 for tax years 2025 through 2027.
valueBasis: $1,000 per child under 4; reduced to $0 at higher incomes
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the New York return with form IT-213.
eligibility: New York resident with a child under 17 at year end; reduced by $16.50 per $1,000 of federal AGI above $75,000 (single or head of household), $110,000 (joint) or $55,000 (married filing separately).
whenNote: A baby born in 2027 counts under 4 on the 2027 return filed in 2028.
catches: File a New York return to get it. The credit for children 4 to 16 is $330 in 2025 and $500 in 2026 and 2027.
notes: One page snippet gave $500 for 2025 ages 4 to 16, others $330; not relevant to newborns.

name: First Step (CollegeInvest)
whatYouGet: A free contribution to a CollegeInvest 529 account for children born or adopted in Colorado on or after Jan 1, 2020.
freeStuff: A free deposit into a 529 account.
valueBasis: Range of award amounts shown in CollegeInvest materials
costDetail: Can open with $0 and fund it with the award.
eligibility: Child born or adopted in Colorado on or after Jan 1, 2020; parent or guardian owns the account; apply before the child's fifth birthday.
whenNote: Apply before the child's fifth birthday.
catches: Official materials show different amounts ($100, $115, $118, $121); confirm on collegeinvest.org. Award arrives within about 30 days of applying.
notes: Amount conflict across official documents, so confidence is low.

name: HSA/FSA money for breast pumps and lactation supplies
whatYouGet: Breast pumps and supplies that assist lactation count as medical expenses, so pre-tax HSA, FSA or HRA money can pay for them.
valueBasis: About 20% to 25% tax saving on a $150 to $300 pump
costDetail: You still pay for the item, using pre-tax money.
eligibility: You need an HSA, FSA or HRA plan. Pub 502 excludes excess bottles for food storage.
whenNote: Often bought in the last weeks of pregnancy or after birth.
catches: The saving is the tax you would have paid, not a free item. Check your plan's own rules before buying.
notes: Pub 502 text confirmed in search results; HSA/FSA use is the IRS reading of Announcement 2011-14 via a secondary summary.

name: Illinois Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A state credit equal to 40% of your Illinois EITC when you have a child under 12 (tax year 2025).
costDetail: No cost; worked out on Schedule IL-E/EITC.
eligibility: You must qualify for the Illinois EITC and have a dependent under 12 on Dec 31.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: No fixed dollar amount, so no value is given. It was 20% of the EITC when first created.

name: Illinois First Steps
whatYouGet: A one-time $50 seed deposit into a Bright Start or Bright Directions 529 account.
freeStuff: $50 deposit into a 529 account.
valueBasis: $50 seed deposit stated by the Treasurer
costDetail: No extra contribution needed.
eligibility: Child born or adopted on or after Jan 1, 2023 to Illinois residents; parent or guardian claims it.
whenNote: Claim before the child's 10th birthday.
catches: Claim before the child's 10th birthday, while opening an account or at brightstart.com/first-steps/claim/. Grandparents cannot claim unless legal guardian.
notes: Claim page URL was named in results; signupUrl is the Bright Start home.

name: Keystone Scholars
whatYouGet: A $100 starter deposit for children born or adopted into Pennsylvania families, created automatically.
freeStuff: $100 deposit into a 529-linked account.
valueBasis: $100 starter deposit stated by the program
costDetail: No cost; no deposit needed.
eligibility: Child born on or after Jan 1, 2019 to Pennsylvania residents, or later adopted by residents.
whenNote: Account appears about 4 to 6 months after birth.
catches: Account is created about 4 to 6 months after birth and a postcard explains how to claim it. Usable from age 18 to 29 if the child has a PA 529 account then.
notes: Out-of-state births take longer. A separate $25 Allegheny County bonus had a Sept 30, 2026 deadline, so it is left out.

name: Maine dependent exemption tax credit (under 6)
whatYouGet: A refundable credit of up to $610 for each child under 6 (twice the $305 base) for tax year 2025.
valueBasis: Up to $610 per child under 6 for tax year 2025; reduced at higher incomes
costDetail: No cost; the worksheet goes with the Maine return.
eligibility: Maine resident or part-year resident; reduced above $100,000 (single), $125,000 (head of household) or $150,000 (joint) per a fiscal note.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: The rule changes for tax years beginning in 2026 and those details were not checked, so the amount for a 2027 birth is unknown. Phase-out thresholds differed slightly between sources.

name: Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay in a benefit year to bond with a new child; benefits have been paid since May 1, 2026.
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Earned at least six times the state average weekly wage in the past year. Pay replaces 90% of wages up to half the state average and a share above that.
whenNote: Application is due in advance when the need is known, or as soon as you know.
catches: The weekly maximum for 2026 and the exact upper-tier rate were not confirmed (results disagree), so no dollar value is given. Whether you can apply before the birth was not confirmed.

name: Massachusetts Child and Family Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A state tax credit of $440 per qualifying dependent under 13 for tax year 2025, with no limit on number of dependents.
valueBasis: $440 per dependent stated in the 2025 Form 1 instructions
costDetail: No cost; claimed on Massachusetts Form 1.
eligibility: Dependent under 13 for federal purposes; file as single, head of household or joint (not married filing separately).
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: Income limits were not in the results.
notes: Signup URL is the state flyer.

name: Massachusetts Paid Family and Medical Leave
brand: Massachusetts Dept. of Family and Medical Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay to bond with a new child; 80% of wages up to half the state average wage plus 50% above that, capped at $1,230.39 a week in 2026.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,230.39 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Massachusetts workers who paid into the program and meet its earnings test. The cap is $1,284.61 in 2027, but a benefit year that starts in 2026 keeps the 2026 cap.
whenNote: Bonding leave must fall within 12 months after the birth.
catches: Payments can be lower if other income or benefits are reported. Application timing was not in the results.

name: Meadowlark savings program
whatYouGet: An automatic one-time $50 deposit into a state-managed account for Nebraska children born in 2020 or later.
freeStuff: $50 deposit set up automatically.
valueBasis: $50 seed deposit stated by the state
costDetail: No cost or paperwork.
eligibility: Child born in Nebraska in 2020 or later.
whenNote: Automatic after the birth is registered.
catches: Funds must be used for qualified higher education costs in Nebraska before age 30. Parents may opt out. The family does not own the account.
notes: Result text said births in 2025 get the deposit in spring; confirm for 2027 births.

name: Minnesota Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A refundable state credit of $1,750 per child under 18 for tax year 2025 ($1,800 in 2026 materials), with no cap on number of children.
valueBasis: Up to $1,750 per child for tax year 2025; reduced above the income threshold
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the Minnesota return.
eligibility: Credit begins to phase out at $31,950 (single) or $37,910 (joint) for 2025; for 2026 at $32,680 or $38,770.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: Higher-income families get a reduced or no credit. The Working Family Credit is separate.
notes: Used the 2025 figure as the modest estimate.

name: Minnesota Paid Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of family leave pay to welcome a new child; most people get 55% to 90% of wages, up to the weekly maximum.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,423 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Earned at least $3,900 in the last year in Minnesota. Weekly maximum is $1,423 in most sources (one source says $1,432); the lower figure is used.
whenNote: You can apply up to 60 days before leave; certification is added after the birth.
catches: Benefits began January 1, 2026. Tell your employer at least 30 days ahead when you can. Medical plus family leave combined is up to 20 weeks.

name: My Alfond Grant
whatYouGet: A $500 grant for babies born to Maine residents, awarded automatically and held for higher education.
freeStuff: $500 grant invested for the child.
valueBasis: $500 grant stated by the program
costDetail: No cost; adding $25 to a NextGen 529 before the first birthday earns a further $100 match.
eligibility: Baby born to Maine residents since Jan 1, 2013. Babies born elsewhere who become Maine residents before age 1 qualify if a NextGen 529 is opened before age 1.
whenNote: Automatic for in-state births; open a NextGen 529 before the first birthday for the match.
catches: The money is invested and may lose value; paid only to eligible schools; forfeited if not used by the child's 28th birthday. The $100 match needs a $25 contribution.
notes: Official FAME and NextGen pages; no application for in-state births.

name: New Baby Match (College SAVE)
whatYouGet: A $200 dollar-for-dollar match when someone puts $200 into a College SAVE account for a North Dakota newborn.
costDetail: The match needs a $200 contribution within 12 months.
eligibility: Newborn up to 12 months old living in North Dakota; one match per child; no income limit; anyone can apply.
whenNote: Contribute within 12 months of enrolling.
catches: Not free: you must contribute $200 first. Subject to available funds; BND may change or stop it. Grant returns to BND if the account sits at zero for six months.
notes: Left value empty because the family has to put in $200 to get $200.

name: New Jersey Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A refundable credit of up to $1,000 per child age 5 or younger for tax year 2025.
valueBasis: $200 to $1,000 per child by taxable income, for tax year 2025
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the New Jersey return.
eligibility: NJ resident with taxable income of $80,000 or less, not filing married separately. Amount by taxable income: $1,000 up to $30,000; $800 to $40,000; $600 to $50,000; $400 to $60,000; $200 to $80,000.
whenNote: Claimed on the state return for the year the child is born.
catches: Part-year residents get a prorated amount.

name: New Jersey Family Leave Insurance
whatYouGet: Pay for up to 12 weeks in one block (or up to 56 days spread out) to bond with a new child, at 85% of average weekly wage up to the maximum.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,119 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Earned at least $310 a week for 20 weeks, or $15,500 in the base year (2026 test). Total benefits are the lesser of 12 times the weekly rate or one-third of base-year earnings.
whenNote: Must be used before the child turns 1 for the 12-week block.
catches: 2026 weekly maximum is $1,119 (up from $1,081 in 2025). Pregnancy and recovery are paid through the separate Temporary Disability program.
notes: Application timing was not in the results.

name: New Mexico Child Tax Credit
brand: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
whatYouGet: A refundable state credit of up to $622 per qualifying child (tax year 2025), larger for lower incomes.
valueBasis: Up to $622 per child (lower of $622 and $637); less at higher incomes
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the New Mexico return (PIT-RC).
eligibility: New Mexico resident with a qualifying child, not a dependent of someone else; the credit shrinks as income rises.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: Results disagree: $622 (January 2026 release) and $637 (state chart); the lower is used. Not limited to young children.

name: New York Paid Family Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay at 67% of average weekly wage, up to a cap, to bond with a new child.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,228.53 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Employed in New York with a covered employer and meeting the program's work-time rules. 2026 weekly maximum is $1,228.53 and total maximum is $14,742.36.
whenNote: Bonding leave can be taken any time in the first 12 months after birth.
catches: Employee contribution in 2026 is 0.432% of gross wages. Pregnancy disability is a separate New York benefit not covered here. Application timing was not in the results.

name: Newborn Social Security number at the hospital
whatYouGet: A free Social Security number and card for your baby, requested while completing the birth certificate at the hospital.
freeStuff: A free Social Security number and card for the baby.
costDetail: Free; SSA says anyone asking for payment is a scam.
eligibility: Baby born in a US hospital; getting a number is voluntary. Providing parents' Social Security numbers is requested but you can apply without both.
whenNote: Request it at the hospital when you give birth certificate information.
catches: Processing time for the card varies by state. Needed for the Child Tax Credit, EITC and the Trump Account deposit.
notes: signupUrl is the main SSA number page; the search did not return it directly, so check it. Limited-edition commemorative cards were issued for births July 2 to Dec 31, 2026, per SSA.

name: Oregon Kids Credit
whatYouGet: A refundable credit of up to $1,050 per child age 5 or younger for tax year 2025 (up to 5 children).
valueBasis: Up to $1,050 per child for tax year 2025; $0 above $31,550
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the Oregon return.
eligibility: Full credit at modified AGI of $26,550 or less, reduced to $0 at $31,550.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: Tax software had errors in early 2026; check the amount. Some state pages still show older figures.

name: Paid Leave Oregon
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay to bond with a child in the first year, plus up to 2 more weeks for pregnancy-related conditions.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,692.16 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Oregon workers who paid into the program. Maximum weekly benefit is $1,692.16 for benefit years starting June 28, 2026 or later; earlier claims keep $1,636.56. Workers earning 65% or less of the state average get 100% of wages.
whenNote: You can apply up to 30 days before leave begins or up to 30 days after it begins.
catches: The extra 2 weeks are for pregnancy conditions, not bonding.

name: Rhode Island Temporary Caregiver Insurance
brand: Rhode Island Dept. of Labor and Training
whatYouGet: Pay for several weeks to bond with a new child in the first 12 months of parenting.
valueBasis: 7 weeks (lower of 7 or 8) at half the $1,103 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: Rhode Island workers who paid into the program and meet its earnings test. Official materials give a weekly maximum of $1,103, rising to $1,150 for benefit years starting July 1, 2026 or later.
whenNote: Bonding claims are allowed only in the first 12 months of parenting.
catches: Official pages disagree on length: the 2026 FAQ says up to 8 weeks, a June 2026 bulletin says 7. The lower figure (7) is used. The $1,150 figure is stated for TDI and applied to TCI by the FAQ.
notes: Confidence low because of the conflict.

name: Rx Kids (Michigan)
whatYouGet: Cash with no strings: $1,500 during pregnancy and $500 a month for 6 months after birth in most communities (some pay 12 months, some only the monthly part).
freeStuff: Cash of $1,500 in pregnancy and $500 a month after birth.
valueBasis: $500 x 6 months at the low end; $1,500 plus $500 x 6 months at the high end
costDetail: Free; paid by direct deposit or prepaid card.
eligibility: Live in a participating community (by where you physically live), be 18 or older (16 to 17 with a guardian's consent), and be at least 16 weeks pregnant or have a baby 6 months or younger born after the community's start date.
region: Participating Michigan cities and counties only
whenNote: Apply from 16 weeks of pregnancy; the $1,500 is lost if you apply after the birth, though monthly payments can still start until the baby is 6 months old.
catches: Only certain communities (for example Flint, Detroit, many Upper Peninsula and other counties); start dates and months paid differ by place. The $1,500 needs an application before the baby is born. You need ID, proof of address and a pregnancy or birth document; staff reply in 2 to 4 weeks and the application is rejected if not verified in 60 days. After birth you fill in another form to start monthly payments.
notes: Results from several county pages were months old; check your community page. Value low end is 6 months only with no prenatal payment.

name: Trump Account $1,000 pilot deposit
whatYouGet: A one-time $1,000 Treasury deposit into a Trump Account for eligible US citizen children born 2025 through 2028.
freeStuff: $1,000 deposited into the child's account by the Treasury.
valueBasis: Pilot deposit of $1,000 stated by the IRS
costDetail: No cost; the election is made with Form 4547.
eligibility: Child born Jan 1, 2025 to Dec 31, 2028, a US citizen with a Social Security number valid for work that was issued before the election, and expected to be a qualifying child of the parent who elects. One pilot election per child.
whenNote: The SSN must be issued before the election. The IRS says if you elect after a qualifying event such as a birth and have already filed your tax return, use the online options at trumpaccounts.gov.
catches: The parent must elect it; it is not automatic even if Treasury enrolls the child. File Form 4547 on the Trump Accounts website or app, in your IRS Individual Online Account, on paper, or with a tax return, and tick the $1,000 pilot box. After the election the trustee contacts you to claim the account and verify identity. For a baby born in 2027 the SSN must exist first, so this follows the birth.
notes: Changed: signupUrl now the IRS Trump Accounts page; account opening confirmed (contributions opened July 4, 2026; election online since mid-2026); added timing and SSN-first rule.

name: Vermont Child Tax Credit
whatYouGet: A fully refundable credit of up to $1,000 per child age 6 or younger for tax year 2025.
valueBasis: Up to $1,000 per child for tax year 2025; reduced above $125,000 AGI
costDetail: No cost; claimed on the Vermont return.
eligibility: Vermont resident; reduced by $20 per $1,000 of AGI above $125,000 and gone at $175,000. A Social Security number or ITIN is not required.
whenNote: Claimed on the return for the year the child is born.
catches: Age limit rose from 5 to 6 for 2025 under Act 71 of 2025.

name: Washington Paid Family and Medical Leave
whatYouGet: Up to 12 weeks of pay to bond with a new child, up to 90% of weekly pay, with a 2026 weekly maximum of $1,647.
valueBasis: 12 weeks at half the $1,647 weekly maximum
costDetail: Funded by payroll contributions; no sign-up fee.
eligibility: At least 820 hours worked in the qualifying period. Up to 16 weeks combined medical and family leave in a claim year, or 18 with pregnancy or birth complications. Minimum benefit is $100 a week in 2026.
whenNote: Bonding leave is for the first year after the birth.
catches: Can be taken in full weeks or intermittently. Application timing was not in the results.

name: BzzAgent
whatYouGet: Community that invites members by email to apply for free product samples from brands, then share an honest review per posting instructions.
costDetail: Participation is free; members are not paid for reviews
eligibility: Must be 18+ (or the age of majority where you live); the platform is operated in the United States.
catches: Per the privacy policy, selection is typically random among qualified applicants when more qualify than there are spots. Reviews and campaign activities are required. The join link on bzzagent.com goes to sampling.powerreviews.com, which is off the bzzagent.com domain (PowerReviews owns BzzAgent). Samples are limited and only chosen applicants get one. Required review and posting per campaign, shared with followers, with disclosure rules. Sponsoring brands may receive info about your participation and act as independent controllers. Privacy notice says it does not sell data for money but shares data with ad/analytics partners, which may count as a sale or share under state law. Campaign invite emails.
notes: Not parenting-specific. Confidence capped at medium because the sign-up step is on another domain.

name: Home Tester Club
whatYouGet: Free to join. Members can apply for free product tests with samples mailed to them, then rate and review them; points are earned for activity. Current campaigns have included children's oral care products.
costDetail: Completely free to join
eligibility: Product tests are matched to member profile; not everyone is selected
catches: Site says it invites its 20 most active members to an exclusive test each month; most members get no test. Not every applicant gets a test. Test partner companies can see your survey answers, written reviews with first name, and photo/video reviews, tied to profile demographics (name, email, phone and address are not shared with them per the policy). Feedback surveys and email after tests. Points have no monetary value.
notes: Not parenting-specific; check the Test page for baby or kids' campaigns.

name: Influenster VoxBox
whatYouGet: Selected members may receive free product boxes (VoxBoxes) to try and review; has a New Parent product category. Not guaranteed.
costDetail: Free to join; boxes go to selected members only
eligibility: Terms bar anyone under 16 from using the service
catches: There is no application for a VoxBox; Influenster picks members based on activity and impact score. Official guide (via search results) says to be eligible for a VoxBox you must sign up and download the app. Not guaranteed a VoxBox; selection depends on activity and impact score. Recipients are expected to post reviews or social content and disclose the product was free. Privacy policy: shares name/last initial/location with third parties who may publish it, shares aggregate data with advertisers, and shares data with partners and service providers; reviews and profile are public. Marketing about specials and new features by email.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. Home page and article pages returned a Cloudflare bot challenge (403), so offer details rest on official-domain search results. Privacy policy and terms pages were read. Not parenting-specific.

name: Moms Meet Sampling Programs
whatYouGet: Approved Mom Ambassadors can apply for free product sampling programs, get a kit mailed, and report back. Current listings are mostly food and kids products.
costDetail: Site says the program is completely free and products are mailed at no cost
eligibility: Only approved Mom Ambassadors or content creators; US residents
catches: Acceptance is not guaranteed; you apply per program and must give feedback. Not baby-specific; open programs seen were food and kids items, and the page may be stale.
notes: Seen only as official-domain search results.

name: Parent Tested Parent Approved (PTPA) Tester Program
whatYouGet: Free to join. Testers are picked from a profile database to receive baby and child products to test, and keep the products.
costDetail: Membership costs nothing; testers keep the product, per the FAQ
eligibility: Matched by profile and each product's criteria; North America
catches: Testers are picked at random from the database; most members are not picked. Selected testers have 24 hours to accept. The profile asks about income, education and children.
notes: Seen only as official-domain search results. Many pages are old; the homepage listed a door-lock test for parents of 0 to 3 year olds.

name: PINCHme
whatYouGet: Apply for free product samples; once qualified for 4 products your box ships free. Feedback on samples unlocks more offers, and extra surveys can earn gift cards.
costDetail: Free to join, no credit card required, box ships free at 4 products
catches: Samples are limited and not guaranteed; the site says they are typically claimed within minutes on release, so most people get few or none. Terms say members are not guaranteed any samples. Privacy policy says information is shared with affiliates, business partners and brand partners for their own business purposes, including direct marketing. Marketing emails about campaigns and offers. Members are asked to share feedback and must follow FTC endorsement disclosure rules.
notes: Not parenting-specific. Terms say membership may be limited by territory and eligibility; the specific rules were not found on the pages read.

name: Tryazon
whatYouGet: Members apply to host parties or receive TryaBoxes of brand products to try, with promised free products per the site.
costDetail: Described as free to try and keep products; sponsor selects participants
eligibility: 18+ (per Terms of Use); US and Canada applicants accepted; sponsors select by demographics such as location, age or number of children
catches: Sponsors choose participants; a limited number of host spots per party. As fetched today, the sign-up form page displayed 'forms are currently under maintenance' and the TryaBox page listed no open opportunities. Applications are shared with the sponsoring brand. FAQ says selection also looks at social accounts and who actively shares, and hosts follow FTC disclosure rules, so expect to post on social media. Privacy policy says it will not sell or rent your information and shares aggregated demographics with partners. Email communications with unsubscribe.
notes: Terms of Use page shows an effective date of May 25, 2018. Specific what-you-get varies by party or TryaBox.
